claims.claim: Activity timeout defaults to 12 hours with a seven-day maximum in D.HH:MM:SS; retries when enabled default to 1 with a 30-second interval; up to 120 activities per pipeline; UponSuccess, UponFailure, UponCompletion and UponSkip branches.
Pipeline expressions use @pipeline().parameters; string interpolation with @{...} always returns a string.

concept_html:
A Data Factory pipeline runs activities: Copy job, notebook, stored procedure, Dataflow, If Condition, ForEach, Until, and more. By default a pipeline holds up to 120 activities. Three settings on each activity decide how a failure behaves (Microsoft Learn, checked September 2026):

  • Timeout. How long an activity may run before it is stopped. The default is 12 hours, and the maximum is seven days, written D.HH:MM:SS. A notebook that normally takes 10 minutes and hangs will hold its slot, and its capacity, for 12 hours unless you lower this.
  • Retry. Retries happen only if you enable them. The retry count then defaults to 1, with 30 seconds between attempts. Retry steps that fail for passing reasons, such as a busy source or a network drop. Do not retry a step that failed because its data is wrong. It will fail again, later.
  • Dependency branches. Each activity connects to the next through a condition: Upon Success, Upon Failure, Upon Completion (either way) or Upon Skip. Put alerts and clean-up on Upon Failure. Upon Completion runs even when the step succeeded.

Parameters and expressions keep one pipeline reusable across sources and environments. Expressions start with @: @pipeline().parameters.wave. Inside a string, @{...} interpolates: "landing/@{pipeline().parameters.wave}/". The result of interpolation is always a string, so "@{pipeline().parameters.max_rows}" passes text, not a number. When a setting needs a number, use the bare expression @pipeline().parameters.max_rows.

Keep business logic out of the pipeline. Transformations belong in notebooks and SQL, where they can be tested (lesson A9-L1). The pipeline decides order, retries and alerts.

exercises.prompt: Write `parse_timeout(value: str) -> int` for a pipeline linter. It parses the `D.HH:MM:SS` format and returns the total seconds. Raise `ValueError` if the format is wrong, if hours are above 23 or minutes or seconds above 59, or if the total exceeds 7 days.
exercises.prompt_html: Write parse_timeout(value: str) -> int for a pipeline linter. It parses the D.HH:MM:SS format and returns the total seconds. Raise ValueError if the format is wrong, if hours are above 23 or minutes or seconds above 59, or if the total exceeds 7 days.
exercises.solution:
import re

TIMEOUT_PATTERN = re.compile(r"(\d+)\.(\d{2}):(\d{2}):(\d{2})")
MAX_SECONDS = 7 * 24 * 3600


def parse_timeout(value: str) -> int:
    """Seconds in a pipeline activity timeout written as D.HH:MM:SS.

    Raises:
        ValueError: On a bad format, out-of-range fields, or more than seven days.
    """
    match = TIMEOUT_PATTERN.fullmatch(value)
    if match is None:
        raise ValueError(f"timeout must be D.HH:MM:SS, got {value!r}")
    days, hours, minutes, seconds = (int(g) for g in match.groups())
    if hours > 23 or minutes > 59 or seconds > 59:
        raise ValueError(f"field out of range in {value!r}")
    total = days * 86400 + hours * 3600 + minutes * 60 + seconds
    if total > MAX_SECONDS:
        raise ValueError("timeout exceeds the seven-day maximum")
    return total

title: Pipelines that fail fast, retry sensibly and alert
why_html: A nightly pipeline ran a 10-minute notebook that sometimes hung on a locked source. With the default 12-hour timeout and no failure branch, each hang held its capacity until mid-morning. Downstream reports showed yesterday's data, and nobody was told. A 30-minute timeout, one retry and an Upon Failure email would have raised the alarm at 02:30 instead of 10:00.
